output.review_comment:
The implementation direction (preserve intentionally mixed-case words like "iPhone"/"McDonald", capitalize first/last word, capitalize small words that begin a subtitle after a colon, otherwise lowercase small words) matches common AP/Chicago-style title-case conventions, so it's not unreasonable on its face. But a few things give me pause and I'd want them addressed before merging:

1. No PR description at all. Given the teammate explicitly said the tests encode an agreed editorial spec, I'd expect the author to state which rule(s) were missing/broken and why this particular set of conditions (`index == 0`, `index == last_index`, `is_after_colon`, "any uppercase after position 0") is the correct generalization — not just that it happens to satisfy the assertions. Right now the three conditions read like they were discovered by iterating on failing test cases one at a time rather than derived from a single documented rule, which is a red flag for overfitting to the test fixtures rather than the actual spec.

2. No confirmation the full suite now passes, and no new tests were added for the edge cases this diff newly handles (mixed-case words, last-word capitalization, colon subtitles). If these behaviors are genuinely part of the agreed spec, they should also be spot-checked with a couple of additional unit tests (which is allowed — only the existing tests are off-limits) to guard against regressions.

3. The `is_mixed_case` branch is very broad: any word with an uppercase letter after position 0 is emitted completely unchanged, including its case, punctuation stripping, and small-word lowering. That means a small word that happens to have mixed casing (e.g., a typo or shouted "OF") would never be lowercased even mid-title, and an ALL-CAPS word would be preserved as-is rather than normalized — that may or may not match what the editorial team wants, but it's a meaningful behavioral decision that should be called out explicitly rather than left implicit in an unexplained diff.

4. `is_after_colon` only checks that the immediately preceding *already-processed* token ends with `:`. That's fine for `"Title: Subtitle"` but silently does nothing for other subtitle delimiters (em dash, semicolon) if the spec intends those too — worth confirming against the actual agreed rules.

Please add a short description of the rule being implemented (ideally referencing the editorial spec), confirm the test suite is green, and consider adding a couple of targeted unit tests for the new branches (mixed-case preservation, last-word capitalization, colon subtitle) so the intent is locked in rather than inferred from the diff.
